en.title: Rio Film Festival Crowns 'The Riverbank' and 'Elza' Top Honors
en.summary: The Rio Film Festival has concluded its latest edition, celebrating cinematic excellence with 'The Riverbank' taking home the Best Fiction Feature Film award and 'Elza' securing Best Documentary Feature Film. The prestigious event highlighted a strong slate of Brazilian cinema.
en.body:
The lights have dimmed on the Rio Film Festival, and the winners are in! Enock Carvalho and Matheus Farias's critically acclaimed **The Riverbank** has officially clinched the Best Fiction Feature Film award, a significant win for the Locarno-winning drama. Meanwhile, Eryk Rocha's **Elza** was honored with the Best Documentary Feature Film prize, capping off a strong showing for Brazilian documentaries.

The awards ceremony, held at the iconic Odeon cinema in Rio de Janeiro, celebrated a rich tapestry of local and international cinema. **The Riverbank**, which is set in Recife and follows a group of young individuals navigating complex social dynamics, has been steadily building acclaim since its premiere. Its win at Rio further solidifies its position as a standout film of the year.

## A Celebration of Brazilian Cinema

Beyond the top fiction and documentary honors, the festival also recognized other significant Brazilian productions. **On Behalf of My Son**, directed by Gabriel Martins, was a major recipient, not only earning accolades but also securing the Fiction Feature – Audience Award. Martins himself was lauded, taking home the Director – Fiction award for his work on the film. This dual recognition underscores the audience's strong connection to the film's narrative and Martins's directorial vision.

Another film making waves was **The French Teacher** (A Professora de Francês), directed by Ricardo Alves Jr. The film, which previously premiered at the San Sebastián Film Festival, earned Grace Passô the Actress – ex aequo award, a testament to her powerful performance. The original score for **The French Teacher** by Florencia Di Concilio also received well-deserved recognition. The festival's commitment to showcasing emerging trends was evident in the Novos Rumos (New Trends) Feature Film award, which went to **Não Estamos Sonhando** by Ulisses Arthur.

## What Audiences Can Expect

The success of films like **The Riverbank** and **On Behalf of My Son** at the Rio Film Festival signals a robust and evolving landscape for Brazilian cinema. These award-winning features, alongside other recognized titles, are likely to gain further international attention and distribution, offering global audiences exciting new stories and perspectives. Fans eager to catch these celebrated films should keep an eye on upcoming festival circuits and potential streaming or theatrical releases in their regions. The festival also recognized achievements in sound design for **The Riverbank**, highlighting the technical artistry involved in these productions.

What's Next

While specific release dates for many of these award-winners are still being finalized, their success at the Rio Film Festival suggests they will be prominent fixtures on the festival circuit and potentially find wider distribution in the coming months. cinephiles worldwide will be eager to experience these acclaimed Brazilian narratives.
